title: Observability for LLM Apps
desc: Build full-stack observability for LLM systems. Learn tracing, metrics, logging, alerting, and the specialized tooling that makes LLM production systems debuggable.
content:
Why LLM Observability is Different

Traditional APM tools track CPU, memory, response times. LLMs add new failure modes: hallucinations, prompt injection, context window overflow, token budget overruns, semantic drift, retrieval failures. You need a new observability stack.

🔭
The 4 Pillars of LLM Observability
Traces: end-to-end request lifecycle (user query → retrieval → LLM → response). Metrics: latency, throughput, cost, cache hit rate. Logs: prompts, completions, errors, token counts. Evals: quality scores (faithfulness, relevance, toxicity) over time. You need all four.

Key Metrics to Track

MetricTypeAlert ThresholdTool
TTFT (p50, p95, p99)Latencyp95 > 2sPrometheus/Grafana
TPOT (tokens/sec)Throughput< 10 tok/svLLM metrics
Request error rateReliability> 1%Any APM
Cost per requestEconomics> budgetHelicone/Langfuse
Token usage (input/output)EconomicsBudget thresholdProvider SDK
Cache hit rateEfficiency< 50%vLLM metrics
Queue depthCapacity> 20vLLM metrics
GPU memory utilizationCapacity> 95%DCGM Exporter
Hallucination rateQuality> 5%Langfuse/Arize

OpenTelemetry for LLMs

OpenTelemetry is the standard for distributed tracing. The LLM ecosystem has standardized on semantic conventions for LLM spans — including token counts, model names, and prompt content.

Python · OpenTelemetry LLM tracing
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.trace import SpanKind

tracer = trace.get_tracer("my-llm-app")

async def call_llm(prompt: str, user_id: str):
    with tracer.start_as_current_span(
        "llm.generation",
        kind=SpanKind.CLIENT,
        attributes={
            "gen_ai.system": "openai",
            "gen_ai.request.model": "gpt-4o",
            "user.id": user_id,
        }
    ) as span:
        response = await llm_call(prompt)
        
        # Record token usage in span
        span.set_attribute("gen_ai.usage.input_tokens",
                            response.usage.prompt_tokens)
        span.set_attribute("gen_ai.usage.output_tokens",
                            response.usage.completion_tokens)
        return response

Setting Up Langfuse

Python · Langfuse tracing
from langfuse import Langfuse
from langfuse.decorators import langfuse_context, observe

langfuse = Langfuse(
    public_key="pk-...",
    secret_key="sk-...",
    host="https://cloud.langfuse.com",
)

# Decorator auto-traces function calls
@observe(name="rag-pipeline")
async def rag_query(question: str):
    # This span is automatically captured
    context = await retrieve(question)
    answer = await generate(question, context)
    
    # Add custom metadata to trace
    langfuse_context.update_current_observation(
        metadata={"num_chunks": len(context), "model": "gpt-4o"},
        tags=["production"],
    )
    return answer

vLLM Metrics with Prometheus + Grafana

vLLM exposes Prometheus metrics out of the box. Set up a full monitoring stack:

YAML · Prometheus scrape config for vLLM
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'vllm'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['vllm-service:8000']
    metrics_path: '/metrics'
    scrape_interval: 15s

# Key vLLM metrics to dashboard:
# vllm:num_requests_running       - active requests
# vllm:num_requests_waiting       - queue depth
# vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc       - VRAM for KV cache
# vllm:e2e_request_latency_seconds - full request time
# vllm:request_prompt_tokens_sum   - input token usage
# vllm:request_generation_tokens_sum - output tokens

GPU Infrastructure Monitoring

Don't forget the underlying hardware. DCGM Exporter (NVIDIA) exports GPU metrics to Prometheus:

  • DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL: GPU compute utilization (%)
  • DCGM_FI_DEV_MEM_COPY_UTIL: Memory bandwidth utilization (%)
  • DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED: VRAM used (bytes)
  • DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE: GPU power draw (watts)
  • DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP: GPU temperature (°C — alert at 85°C)
  • DCGM_FI_DEV_NVLINK_BANDWIDTH_TOTAL: NVLink inter-GPU traffic

SLOs for LLM Applications

Define your Service Level Objectives before you go to production. LLM SLOs differ from traditional services:

SLOTargetMeasurement
TTFT (p95)< 1 secondPer-request latency from request start to first token
Token throughput> 50 tok/s per replicaOutput tokens / wall time per request
Availability99.9%Successful responses / total requests
Cost per request< $0.01Token cost + compute cost / request
Quality (faithfulness)> 90%LLM-as-judge or human evaluation sample
🚨
Alert Runbook
Queue depth > 20 → scale out. GPU cache > 95% → reduce max_model_len or add replicas. TTFT p95 > 2s → check if single slow request is blocking (chunked prefill fixes this). Error rate > 1% → check if model OOMed, check vLLM logs for preemptions. Cost spike → check for prompt injection making context very long.
🔑
Key Takeaways
1. Start with Langfuse (free, self-hostable) for traces and Prometheus + Grafana for infrastructure metrics. 2. Always track TTFT, TPOT, token costs, and queue depth at minimum. 3. GPU monitoring via DCGM Exporter is non-negotiable for production. 4. Define SLOs before launch — you can't know if you're meeting targets if you haven't defined them. 5. LLM quality eval (faithfulness, relevance) must be automated; manual review doesn't scale.
🎉
